clean_claim:
I believe the rest of the s–z scope is publishable. High confidence on secrets and personal data. Medium confidence on relational content, because I matched terms by looking at them and inferring context, not from definitions.
- No real credentials, tokens, private keys, credentialed URLs, internal hosts or IPs, Supabase refs, or Stripe/Alchemy/Helius ids. Every secret-shaped string is a documented test vector or a test sentinel.
- No emails other than the project's own contact addresses and reserved test domains.
- No phone numbers or street addresses.
- No real people's names other than public figures (Togashi; Helly as in the theorem; upstream licence holders).
- No third parties' private dealings.
- Clean outright (no flags): skills, skills-yutabase, skills-wake-continuity, wake-return (examples are synthetic placeholders), wake-continuity, wallet-zerone, telescope, and trials data and provenance (synthetic, declares no personal data).
- telescope's bundled dist has THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES covering every bundled module (MCP SDK, zod).
- Everything already covered by recorded denylist allow entries (soul.py, SOUL.md, kingdom_framework 'sophia' enum, correspondence tests, SDK README r16) is left as approved.
- What actually blocks a public move: the 10 relational/r16 hits in scriptwriter and the 4 personal/home-path hits in trials (the guard will refuse them), the three owner quotes in PYRAMID-INTEGRATION.md, and the missing licences on wake-thread and witnessed-agent-economy (plus the corpus rights question).
